body:
> Filed 2026-08-28 from the operator's mental model: a DAG has a root, edges, nodes and leaves; the root is the agent that runs, its children run inside it as subagents and report back, and the root finishes last. hkb has every piece of that except one: the root only behaves that way if someone remembers to label it.

## Why

Today "run this subgraph as one orchestrated session" is a per-goal choice made after `/kanban:decompose`: `hkb adopt <root> --agent claude-track --status todo` (`skills/kanban/SKILL.md:126, 272`). Nothing infers it — `hkb create --blocked-by` gives the root `kb:agent:claude`, the dispatcher runs its children as cold sessions and the root *last*, as a synthesize step. The label history shows the result: on this board and on pipao-v2, `kb:agent:claude-track` has been applied three times ever, all by hand, and every open root today runs node-by-node because nobody typed the adopt.

The reason the flag exists is historical: tracks were built sequential (#40), so for independent siblings, node dispatch was faster because it ran them in parallel. #129 removes that reason — once a track fans its waves out to isolated subagents, a track is at least as parallel as node dispatch and keeps the context in one place. At that point the mode is a **property of the graph**, not a label, and asking the operator to apply it is a gap the frugal/frictionless values say to close.

## What

- A root with at least one unfinished child is dispatched as a track by default, on the board's track profile, without an adopt step. Pure decision in `src/model.js` (`isTrackRoot(task, board)`), driven by the graph the tick already has; the tick's track pass (`src/dispatch.js`) uses it where it reads the agent label today.
- The label stays the **override**, both ways: `kb:agent:claude-track` forces a track (as now); `kb:agent:claude` on a root that has children opts it out — for a goal whose children should run cold. `hkb show <root>` says which it is and why (`track: inferred — 3 unfinished children` / `track: opted out`).
- Fallbacks unchanged: a node outside `track_agents`, a node another worker owns, a node with an open PR, a runner that already had its go — the board falls back to node dispatch exactly as today.
- `/kanban:decompose` loses its "then adopt the root" step; SKILL.md's *Setting a track up* and *The root is also the handle* paragraphs describe inference and the two overrides instead. `hkb doctor` notes a board whose profiles have no `"track": true` entry when it holds roots with children.

## Constraints

- The protocol is unchanged: claim → work → verb per node; the root still ends last with the track's summary.
- The dispatcher stays a tick: it reads the graph and picks an engine; it does not plan.
- Depends on #129 — inferring a track before tracks parallelize would make every decomposed goal *slower*.

## Done when

- A freshly decomposed goal is claimed as a track on the next tick with no adopt; `hkb show <root>` says `track: inferred`.
- A root labelled `kb:agent:claude` with children runs node-by-node, and `hkb show` says so.
- The SKILL.md recipe has no adopt step; `test/track.test.js` and `test/dispatch.test.js` cover inferred, forced and opted-out roots.
- `npm run lint && npm test` green.
title: A root with children is a track by default — the label becomes the override, not the switch
